new.name: Gemini 4 Carbon
new.why: NEW: Google’s strongest model, two weeks after Argon, built for multi-day coding and cyber-defence work. Google says it tops the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5 at 59 (vendor-cited). Cyber experts get it first through the Fairwind programme; same introductory price as Argon, $2/$10 per million tokens.

new.name: GPT-6.1 Terra
new.why: NEW: OpenAI’s fast, cheaper model for computer use and everyday work, at 50% lower standard API prices than GPT-5.6 Terra. OpenAI says it matches GPT-6 Astra on its agents test at a tenth of the per-token price (vendor-reported). Rated ‘Critical’ for cyber, so Astra’s protections apply.

new.name: Kimi K3.1 Pro
new.why: NEW: a 2.8-trillion-parameter mixture-of-experts model (104B active, 1M-token context), launched in Kimi’s apps and API and then released as open weights. Its custom licence restricts large model-as-a-service use.

new.name: Muse Spark Open
new.why: NEW: open weights for an 816B-parameter (42B active), natively multimodal model with a 1M-token context, which Meta calls the most capable US open-weight model. It can run on two Apple M5 Ultra Mac Studios; the Muse Model License limits commercial use.

new.name: Mistral Large 4 (open weights)
new.why: NEW: the 1-trillion-parameter multimodal ‘Le Chonk’ went from API preview (6 Oct) to open weights on Hugging Face after three more weeks of training. Mistral reports Terminal-Bench 4.0 rising from 28% to 41% (vendor-reported); a quantised version runs on four B200 or B300 GPUs.

new.name: DeepInfer
new.why: NEW: DeepSeek open-sourced (Apache 2.0) the inference engine that runs its own production service, for Nvidia SM100 and Huawei Ascend 950 chips. It supports only V4.1-Flash for now and leaves out caching and load balancing; the speed figures are DeepSeek’s own. Its repository passed 25,000 stars in its first 24 days.

new.name: Tencent Hy4
new.why: NEW: Tencent’s latest model adds image understanding and computer use for the first time, at $0.834/$2.501 per million tokens. Tencent says weights and a system card will follow ‘in the coming days’; as of 9 Nov they were not out.

new.name: Genie 4
new.why: NEW: a world model that generates interactive scenes you can steer in plain language while they run, now with native audio and dialogue. It is a research preview for trusted testers, coming next to AI Ultra subscribers in Project Genie.

new.name: GPT-6 Cyber
new.why: NEW: a GPT-6 model for authorised vulnerability research, offered only to vetted defenders through OpenAI’s Daybreak programme, not to the public.

new.name: ChatGPT Images 2.6
new.why: NEW: ChatGPT can now turn a prompt or photo into an animated GIF, edit single frames, and keep saved reference images of people, pets or characters for reuse. Available on all plans, free included; OpenAI says over 4 billion images a week are now made with its tools.

new.name: Siri AI (opened to all developers)
new.why: NEW: any app can now plug into the rebuilt Siri through a developer preview in the iOS 27.3 betas. Apple has also dropped the waitlist for users, but caps server-side use daily and plans a fee for more; Siri AI is still unavailable in the EU on iPhone.

new.name: Grok Bot
new.why: NEW to the board: the agent that runs tasks on its own virtual computer launched in August, but this window tested its economics. SpaceX said it had over 800,000 paid weekly users; on 1 Nov Musk said serving costs were ‘unsustainably high relative to revenue’ as weekly limits ran out early. It gained phone calls on 4 Nov.

new.name: Gemini app: Argon and tasks
new.why: NEW: Pro and Ultra subscribers got Gemini 4 Argon in the app, plus a toggle from chat to ‘tasks’ that keeps working while you are away, connections to more than 40 apps (Instacart, OpenTable, Shopify) and Antigravity coding in the Mac app.

new.name: dsh-superagent (research prototype)
new.why: NEW: an MIT-licensed, always-on coding agent for one GitHub repository that picks up requests from GitHub or Feishu, works in its own session and answers with a pull request. DeepSeek calls it research code, not a product, and warns a worker can read the operator’s home directory. Fastest-rising repository on this edition’s radar.

carryover_updates.name: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017
carryover_updates.why: UPDATED: a new snapshot of September’s V4.1-Flash, now the default behind DeepSeek’s API, with open weights on Hugging Face. DeepSeek claims better benchmarks with shorter outputs (vendor-reported); it also opened web search and fetch APIs at $0.75 per 1,000 calls.

carryover_updates.name: Gemini 4 Argon
carryover_updates.why: UPDATED: no longer limited to cyber partners. Developers can use it on the paid Gemini API, AI Studio and Antigravity, and Pro and Ultra subscribers in the Gemini app, from 13 Oct.

carryover_updates.name: Dots
carryover_updates.why: UPDATED: dots can now be created on the phone (9 Oct), answered from an iPhone notification and run on GPT-6.1 Terra; on 4 Nov they reached eligible Enterprise, Edu and Healthcare workspaces, free in an admin preview until billing starts on 18 Nov.

retire.name: GPT-6 Astra
retire.reason: Predates the window (3 Sep); OpenAI's newer releases (GPT-6.1 Terra, GPT-6 Cyber) replace it on the board, though it remains OpenAI's top model.

retire.name: Grok 4.7
retire.reason: No new development found in the window.

retire.name: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
retire.reason: Superseded by the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 snapshot (carried over).

retire.name: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
retire.reason: August release; no new development found in the window.

retire.name: Qwen3.8-Max (open weights)
retire.reason: August release; no new development found in the window.

retire.name: Muse personal agent
retire.reason: 8 Sep launch with no material consumer update found in the window; Meta's open-weight Muse Spark Open is on the foundation board instead.

retire.name: Gemini Spark
retire.reason: No update found in the window; the Gemini app's new tasks mode (13 Oct) is on the board instead. Spark's $99.99/mo price was single-source.

retire.name: GitHub Copilot (unified)
retire.reason: The merge was due from late September; no new development found in the window (group B may cover Copilot under coding).

notes: Missed by the 9 Oct refresh and not added, because they predate this window: Claude Opus 5.5 (22 Sep), Claude Sonnet 5.5 (28 Sep), GPT-6.1 Sol (29 Sep), Claude Haiku 5.5 (7 Oct) and GPT-6 with Intelligent UI in ChatGPT (7 Oct).

Dates that differ between sources: GPT-6.1 Terra (OpenAI's launch posts 26 Oct; one model-tracking site lists 15 Oct); Kimi K3.1 Pro weights (Moonshot's post 4 Nov; one roundup says 5 Nov); Tencent Hy4 (Tencent 4 Nov; Artificial Analysis 3 Nov).
Mistral Large 4 active parameters: Mistral's 6 Oct post on X says 49B, while its blog and TNW give about 52B for the released model.
Tencent Hy4 is described as open source, but its weights were not out by 9 Nov; Artificial Analysis lists it as proprietary for now.
Single-source figures: Grok Bot's 800,000+ paid weekly users (SpaceX, via Business Insider) and the Siri AI waitlist removal (Yahoo Tech).

All benchmark figures on these cards are the vendors' own. Model-tracking aggregators (nocode.mba, llmbenchmark.ai, benchlm.ai) were used only to find releases; every card links a first-party page or a GitHub repository.
Name-collision watch: 'Muse' is Meta's consumer agent, also its Muse Spark model family and its Muse Code tool. Grok Bot posts from the @bot account on X. xAI now trades as SpaceXAI.
dsh-superagent-prototype is filed under agentic; dedupe it against group B's cards. DeepInfer sits with the foundation models because it is DeepSeek's serving stack for V4.1-Flash.
Not carded: GPT-6 Cyber's details beyond limited Daybreak access, Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash (video, 5 Nov), and the long tail of smaller October releases (MiniMax M3.1 Flash, Nemotron 3.5, Liquid d1).
